title: recording
description: A specific narration/production of a work: narrators, abridged flag, runtime, chapters, publisher(s), and region-scoped identifiers. One production released in several marketplaces stays ONE recording: the region rides on the identifier (asin[], the object form of isbn[]) and on publishers[], never on a second record.

narrators.description: The recording's narrators as person slugs. The slug is the identity, so the list may not repeat one.

abridged.description: Whether this narration is abridged. Optional: absence means unknown, so importers omit it rather than guessing.

publisher.description: The publisher of record for this production. One production can be issued by a different imprint in another marketplace; those go in publishers[], and this field stays the one the record leads with.

publishers.description: OTHER regions' imprints of this same production, one entry per region. It never restates the top-level publisher (that fact already has a home) and never repeats a region. Emitted only when a source STATED a regional publisher - absence means nothing is known about that marketplace, not that the publisher of record covers it. It REQUIRES publisher (see dependentRequired): "the other regions" is meaningless without the one it is other than, and a record carrying publishers[] with no publisher is a trap - the next enrichment run fills the absent field from a row, which can be a name already in this list, minting the restatement pkg/check refuses. The dependency turns that into a schema error at compose time rather than a validation failure after the write.

isbn.description: This recording's ISBNs. An entry has exactly one of two forms, and they mix freely in one list: a bare STRING is an ISBN whose region is unstated, and the OBJECT {isbn, region} is used ONLY when the region IS known - one production released in several marketplaces carries different identifiers, and this is how the second one is recorded without minting a second recording. Both properties are required in the object form, so an unstated region has exactly one spelling and canonical form stays unambiguous. The bare string is not merely the shape that predates regions: it is the SCALE form. No bulk writer emits anything else (no import source states the marketplace an ISBN belongs to, and the issue forms contribute a scoped entry one at a time), and across 142k recordings one canonical line beats the object's four against the pack size caps - which is what enrichment filling ISBNs in bulk will spend. The region-scoped form earns its four lines by stating a fact nothing else can.

audio_url.description: The audio file this chapter IS, for a recording published as one file per section (LibriVox: the archive.org MP3). Only a LibriVox recording carries it today, so pkg/check requires librivox_id beside it.

readers.description: Who reads THIS chapter, as person slugs, each one of the recording's narrators (pkg/check). A LibriVox section's: pkg/check requires librivox_id beside it. Written for a recording whose chapters are read by different people (a LibriVox collaborative project): when no chapter of the recording carries readers, who reads which chapter is unstated, except that a recording with one narrator is read by them throughout; once any chapter carries them, a chapter without them states no reader.

section_number.description: The source's own number for this chapter (LibriVox: section_number), written only where it differs from the chapter's 1-based position - LibriVox numbers some projects from 0, and a few from a later volume's first section. Absent means the position IS the number. Only a LibriVox recording carries it today, so pkg/check requires librivox_id beside it and refuses a value equal to the position (one fact, one spelling).

librivox_id.description: The LibriVox project id this recording IS. The identity a LibriVox import deduplicates on (never the title); unique across the dataset (pkg/check).

archive_id.description: The Internet Archive item identifier holding this recording's files (archive.org/details/<archive_id>).

links.description: Where the recording is published, as the source stated each URL: its catalogue page (librivox), a zip of every file (zip), its podcast feed (rss), the text it reads from (text), and its product page in a store that sells it outside the identifier-derived retailers (audiobookguild, graphicaudio). https only; pkg/check holds each store key to that store's own host and each store URL unique across the dataset.

text.description: The text the recording reads from, as the source states it (LibriVox: url_text_source).

audiobookguild.description: The recording's product page on the Audiobook Guild store (audiobookguild.com), as the store states it. A volatile route rather than an identifier: a dead link is a data edit.

graphicaudio.description: The recording's product page on the GraphicAudio store (graphicaudio.net), as the store states it. A volatile route rather than an identifier: a dead link is a data edit.

librivox_title.description: The LibriVox project's own title, exactly as LibriVox states it - its repeat markers ("(version 2)", "(Dramatic Reading)") and its spelling kept. The work's title is the work's (a project attached to a catalogued work reads in the catalogue's spelling, its markers stripped); this is the project's, which the LibriVox-shaped feed answers with. Requires librivox_id (pkg/check).

librivox_genres.description: The LibriVox project's own genre names, verbatim and in LibriVox's order, each once (LICENSING.md's public-domain exception). They are a fact about the LibriVox project, never the work's genres: the work's genres stay this project's vocabulary, mapped in code. The LibriVox-shaped feed answers and filters ?genre= with them. Requires librivox_id (pkg/check).

credits.description: Contributors credited on THIS recording in a role that is not narration. Today one role: the translator of the translation a LibriVox project reads, a fact about the project (two LibriVox translations of one work credit two different translators). It is ADDITIONAL to the work's own credits, never instead of them: a work keeps the translator credits its sources stated, and authors stays the identity list. The (person, role) shape and rules of a work's credits, the people resolving into the people family, but only the roles a recording can state (`translator`); a role is added here by schema change when a source states one per production. Optional; written only when the source STATED the role. A LibriVox import writes them in LibriVox's order; pkg/check requires librivox_id beside them.

copyright_year.description: The copyright year of the text this recording reads, as the source stated it (LibriVox: copyright_year; its 0, meaning unstated, is never written). Negative for a year BC. A fact about the recorded text, deliberately not the work's first_published, which another source may own.

added_at.description: When this recording entered the database. Stamped at creation by the importer and the intake bot as a plain date; records dated by the one-time git-history backfill carry that commit's full timestamp verbatim. Optional, since records predating the field carry none.
